observations: The native Reader raw output has a broad arc/ring around a dark centre in the right half, at the position of the published known-letter overlay. The left half contains a broad lower bright response at the other known-letter location.
The median-to-p99.5 display exposes the same raw response locations and suppresses the diffuse grey background; it does not add an independently resolved stroke.

Two upper narrow prongs apparent in the published left known-letter overlay are not separated with comparable clarity in this Reader output. The right response looks more continuously closed around its dark centre than parts of the published overlay; without independent pixel ground truth this is not labelled an invented character.

In the shared old 256-square view Reader retains a connected curved response where the saved Hecate view shows disconnected blobs. Dense-native also shows part of the curve. Native spacing/depth/checkpoint/context and display windows differ, so this is not a controlled claim of superior model accuracy.
decision: Known partial stroke/shape reproduction is sufficient to justify one bounded Reader V3 test on an unread surface; character transcription and complete individual letter recovery are not established here.
limits: This is known published text, not a discovery.
Model-family novelty and training holdout/generalization have not been established.
Raw output and display transform are distinguished; no claim that every bright pixel is ink.
